newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian premier Vaehi formally resigns - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Estonian premier Vaehi formally resigns - spokesman.

text.p: Estonian Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi went to see President Lennart Meri on Tuesday to formally hand in his resignation, Vaehi's spokesman said.
The move comes some two weeks after Vaehi announced he would quit.
The president now has 14 days to choose a successor to Vaehi, who had weathered two previous government crises to stay in power since early 1995.
Political parties have already identified their preferred candidate for premier as Mart Siiman, the head of the parliamentary faction of Vaehi's Coalition Party.
Despite frequent political turmoil under Vaehi, Estonia has managed to pursue the economic reforms launched after the small Baltic state quit the former Soviet Union in 1991.
Siiman had a career in television and radio both in the Soviet-era and after Estonia regained its indepence before becoming a politician.
